body:
Author: Pyro <Valderrey@email.msn.com>
Date: 1999/07/27

> Enough of the blather.  We know what political correctness is, and
> those who vehemently deny its existance even moreso.  Political
> correctness is presuming that you are "automatically right" because
> your opinion or view holds greater emotional appeal than your
> counterparts.  The politically correct elite have also instilled
> within the public the notion, that those who challenge the core
> beliefs that they propagate are evil, wicked, and have comitted SIN.

   Yes, this paragraph seems agreeable until you reach the last few
 words.  It would be an overstatement to claim that such elements as
 "evil" and "sin" are fictions propagated by a "politically correct
 elite" and/or -only- by them.  Ridding ourselves of such "politically
 correct elite" would not eliminate "sin" but instead wreck havoc on
 attempts to discern what such terms could mean.  Someone's claim of a
 word without meaning (for them) doesn't invalidate another's search for
 meaning, and if "evil" or "sin" really don't have meaning then there'd
 be nothing lost if that putative "absense of meaning" were re-verified.
 The existence of manipulative propaganda on the part of a media elite
 doesn't disprove an underlying reality which may or may not conform to
 their highly questionable and not-so-sublimated subliminal agenda.

   It may, furthermore, be critical to take cognizance of the fact that
 when stating "... _we_know_ what political correctness is..." there is
 still nothing implied which asserts the knowledge as being -coherent-,
 i.e. the definition applied by one individual may not necessarily be
 in correspondence with another's definition, because each individual
 might independently assert personal claims to a certain aspect of PC.
 Thereby, something is intrinsically faulty when abiding in "knowledge"
 traced to inherent solipsism. (see: _Personal_Identity_, J.Perry, ed)


> _Politically_Incorrect_ is not a forum for vigorous discussion.  The
> show is a front for the elites to say, "you see, PC really is a joke,
> and we can talk about all issues openly." The reality is, the more
> serious issues involving politically correct repression are not dealt
> with on the show.

    Also much agreement here:  do viewers take note of that show's
  frequent commercial interruptions?    :-)  :-)  :-)


> Larry King clever? Yes, clever for having a closet PC'er pretending
> to be representative of the masses of repressed non-PC'ers, and being
> able to shut down the opposition with their superficial, tendentious
> discourse.

    Ah yes, and clever because Larry King is unabashedly PC.


> Science requires objectivity.  We can theorize all that we want, can
> even come to believe that dinosaurs and humans lived side by side, but
> that does not change reality.  Of course, PC'ers can continue to
> believe that blacks, whites, and Asians have _equal_ intellectual
> potential, that they all have _equal_ athletic ability, that whites
> can be great pugilists too, but blacks have succeeded
> disproportionately simply because they tried harder, having been
> been excluded from the professions.

    Group inequalities are stipulated herein, but unless you're willing
  to dispute _Brown_vs._Board_of_Education_ (1954), a legal precendent
  exists which asserts economic benefit to the nation via desegregation.


> But when PC'ers begin to impede on the rights on non-PC'ers I am going
> to raise a fuss.  When the head of the psychology department at the
> University of Delaware tells Linda Gottfredson that she cannot receive
> funds to study innate differences among the races because it is
> "racist", someone has to blow the horn.  PC'ers can believe in the
> tooth fairy for all I care, but when they work on hindering the rights
> of people who seek the truth, when it happens to conflict with their
> fairy-tale utopic vision, I will have to protest.

   I admit to some confusion here.  Weren't you about to posit a claim
 that racial differences had already been established, and sufficient
 evidence already published?  If so, why the additional duplication from
 Ms. Gottfredson?  I thought affirmative action programs were premised
 upon acceptance of racial variations, even as terms of "race/ethnicity"
 aren't clearly defined (example: "Caucasians" can claim 'black' ethnic
 affiliation if disadvantaged by being raised within a black ghetto).

   Next, you've provided a characterization of what the term "PC" might
 entail, in "presuming one is automatically right," yet while you do
 that you are nonetheless quick on the draw to assert "rights" without
 any documentation in law literature, e.g. "rights of non-PC'ers" who by
 definition, were -absent- any statement of being "automatically right."
 Perhaps we'll need to sharpen our discussion on this point:  the First
 Amendment Right is not constructed upon analysis of whether someone is
 or is not "PC" but upon constitutional rights of minorities against an
 unjust oppression by the majority.  A "PC" attribute might not fall so
 neatly along the lines of being or not being a member of a minority or
 the majority, particularly in context to where boundary gerrymandering
 was drawn, from which the notions of "minority/majority" got extracted.

   If we're to run with a notion that "non-PC'ers" are not automatically
 right then it's incumbent upon "non-PC'ers" to sustain their burden of
 proof at each step in the argument, a burden they should be eager and
 -willing- to obtain since "not being automatically right" was their
 existential condition, according to your provided characterization.


> I was merely pointing out that we all have innate tendencies which
> influence how we end up, the ideas we come to accept. It is well known
> among psychologists that "liberals" and "conservatives" _think_
> differently. That's not to say we have absolutely no free will, or
> ability to drastically change our core beliefs. I am just pointing out
> that, in my opinion, genetics may play a role in influencing the
> belief system we come to accept. Capiche?

    If you'd say that "ability to drastically change our core beliefs"
  is also an "innate tendency" then the "innate tendencies" are not
  immutable, even without genetic mutation and genetic bioengineering.
  First you're asserting (as fact?) that "we all have innate tendencies
  which influence how we end up..." but later you state this as simply
  your "opinion" so which case is it going to be?


<< Was TK a fascist? >>
> Honestly, I don't think so.  But I believe he has tendencies toward
> fascism. I believe he has even contacted Dr. Pierce in the past.

    Yet TK's manifesto specifically invokes "non-political revolution."
  How could he possibly be a (political) fascist?

         "4. We therefore advocate a revolution against the industrial
         system.  This revolution may or may not make use of violence:
         it may be sudden or it may be a relatively gradual process
         spanning a few decades. We can't predict any of that. But we
         do outline in a very general way the measures that those who
         hate the industrial system should take in order to prepare the
         way for a revolution against that form of society. This is not
         to be a POLITICAL revolution. Its object will be to overthrow
         not governments but the economic and technological basis of
         the present society."


> << I think you'll need to restart your analytical engine: opposition
> to High-Technology is an opposition to fascism, and opposition to all
> forms of social controls so popular with fascists that were enabled
> by means of High-Technological spying and privacy infringements. >>

> Oh, please. Ask the Polish who were more oppressive: the communists or
> fascists? I have an uncle who left socialist Cuba to fascist Spain,
> and came to admire Generalissimo Franco.  Now before you spew a
> bromidic retort, he happens to be married to a woman who is part
> black, and has no feelings of racism.  He also has 4 degrees.

  Fine -- now here's the bromidic retort as expected:

    Any totalitarian state can be serviced by that High-Technology TK
  identifies as their core means of asserting social controls over the
  masses, from the left or right.  The fact that your uncle who was not
  documented in Poland, nor in TK's manifesto, and has no necessary
  bearing upon your own views nor upon this exchange, admired defunct
  facists from a safe distance, has a trophy wife by way of chic racial
  tokenism, and allows you brief non-racist respite coupled with that
  obvious inspiration toward sheepskin appropriation and other sundry
  "golden fleece" awards, says nothing about the itemized sub-point to
  this particular thread, i.e. opposition to fascism (a special case of
  totalitarian regimes in general) follows from opposition to forms of
  High-Technological encroachment upon imaginative freedoms.

         "... But what kind of freedom does one have if one can use it
         only as someone else prescribes? FC's conception of freedom is
         not that of Bolivar, Hu, Chang or other bourgeois theorists.
         The trouble with such theorists is that they have made the
         development and application of social theories their surrogate
         activity. Consequently the theories are designed to serve the
         needs of the theorists more than the needs of any people who
         may be unlucky enough to live in a society on which the
         theories are imposed."

  Conservatives do not improve upon that quest for freedom by "the
  average individual" because they simply promote "the power of Big
  Business" by whipping up resentment against "Big Government" --

         "13. (Paragraph 66) Conservatives' efforts to decrease the
         amount of government regulation are of little benefit to the
         average man. For one thing, only a fraction of the regulations
         can be eliminated because most regulations are necessary. For
         another thing, most of the deregulation affects business
         rather than the average individual, so that its main effect is
         to take power from the government and give it to private
         corporations. What this means for the average man is that
         government interference in his life is replaced by
         interference from big corporations, which may be permitted,
         for example, to dump more chemicals that get into his water
         supply and give him cancer. The conservatives are just taking
         the average man for a sucker, exploiting his resentment of Big
         Government to promote the power of Big Business."


> << TK's demolition of the right is much harsher than his supposed
> (ironic) "literary criticism" of left-leftism. >>

> You have absolutely no clue. TK spent a great portion of the Manifesto
> bashing political correctness and leftism.  He bashed people like you,
> who enjoy playing semantics and spewing superfluous drivel rather than
> to cut to the issues.  The one measly sentence in which he referred to
> conservatives as "fools" has given trolls like you justification for
> pretending he was leftist all along.  The real world isn't black and
> white, you know.

     He said the revolution he advocates is -similar- to the French and
   Russian revolutions, which each were leftist:

         "181. As we stated in paragraph 166, the two main tasks for
         the present are to promote social stress and instability in
         industrial society and to develop and propagate an ideology
         that opposes technology and the industrial system. When the
         system becomes sufficiently stressed and unstable, a
         revolution against technology may be possible. The pattern
         would be similar to that of the French and Russian
         Revolutions. French society and Russian society, for several
         decades prior to their respective revolutions, showed
         increasing signs of stress and weakness. Meanwhile, ideologies
         were being developed that offered a new world view that was
         quite different from the old one. In the Russian case,
         revolutionaries were actively working to undermine the old
         order. Then, when the old system was put under sufficient
         additional stress (by financial crisis in France, by military
         defeat in Russia) it was swept away by revolution. What we
         propose in something along the same lines."


     He mentioned that "true believers" of either form -- leftists or
   (rightwing) nazis -- presented "a problem" and would not "make a
   safe recruit to the revolution" particularly if he is "committed
   also to _another_ ideal" (such as some racially eugenic agenda):

         "222. Leftists, especially those of the oversocialized type,
         are True Believers in the sense of Eric Hoffer's book, "The
         True Believer." But not all True Believers are of the same
         psychological type as leftists.  Presumably a truebelieving
         nazi, for instance is very different psychologically from a
         truebelieving leftist. Because of their capacity for
         single-minded devotion to a cause, True Believers are a
         useful, perhaps a necessary, ingredient of any revolutionary
         movement.  This presents a problem with which we must admit we
         don't know how to deal. We aren't sure how to harness the
         energies of the True Believer to a revolution against
         technology. At present all we can say is that no True Believer
         will make a safe recruit to the revolution unless his
         commitment is exclusively to the destruction of technology. If
         he is committed also to another ideal, he may want to use
         technology as a tool for pursuing that other ideal (see
         paragraphs 220, 221)."


     He's clearly opposed to "eugenics" because that would amount to an
   unnatural "manufactured product," additional "government regulation,"
   and the (arbitrary) imposition of "medical ethics" determined by some
   'elite' scientific soviet, or "needs of the industrial-technological
   system."  So TK would thereby be opposed to racial goals concurrent
   with either "eugenic" or "dis-eugenic" agendas:

         "122. Even if medical progress could be maintained without the
         rest of the technological system, it would by itself bring
         certain evils.  Suppose for example that a cure for diabetes
         is discovered. People with a genetic tendency to diabetes will
         then be able to survive and reproduce as well as anyone else.
         Natural selection against genes for diabetes will cease and
         such genes will spread throughout the population. (This may be
         occurring to some extent already, since diabetes, while not
         curable, can be controlled through the use of insulin.) The
         same thing will happen with many other diseases susceptibility
         to which is affected by genetic degradation of the population.
         The only solution will be some sort of eugenics program or
         extensive genetic engineering of human beings, so that man in
         the future will no longer be a creation of nature, or of
         chance, or of God (depending on your religious or
         philosophical opinions), but a manufactured product.

         "123. If you think that big government interferes in your life
         too much NOW, just wait till the government starts regulating
         the genetic constitution of your children. Such regulation
         will inevitably follow the introduction of genetic engineering
         of human beings, because the consequences of unregulated
         genetic engineering would be disastrous.  [19]

         "124. The usual response to such concerns is to talk about
         'medical ethics.' But a code of ethics would not serve to
         protect freedom in the face of medical progress; it would only
         make matters worse. A code of ethics applicable to genetic
         engineering would be in effect a means of regulating the
         genetic constitution of human beings.  Somebody (probably the
         upper-middle class, mostly) would decide that such and such
         applications of genetic engineering were "ethical" and others
         were not, so that in effect they would be imposing their own
         values on the genetic constitution of the population at large.
         Even if a code of ethics were chosen on a completely
         democratic basis, the majority would be imposing their own
         values on any minorities who might have a different idea of
         what constituted an "ethical" use of genetic engineering. The
         only code of ethics that would truly protect freedom would be
         one that prohibited ANY genetic engineering of human beings,
         and you can be sure that no such code will ever be applied in
         a technological society. No code that reduced genetic
         engineering to a minor role could stand up for long, because
         the temptation presented by the immense power of biotechnology
         would be irresistible, especially since to the majority of
         people many of its applications will seem obviously and
         unequivocally good (eliminating physical and mental diseases,
         giving people the abilities they need to get along in today's
         world). Inevitably, genetic engineering will be used
         extensively, but only in ways consistent with the needs of the
         industrial-technological system. [20]"

   So we're not dealing with "one measly sentence" but a constellation
 of antipathies attached to the prospect of right-wing fascism.  Even
 if the "real world" isn't Black and White, TK's manifesto asks of the
 reader to consider the portion that might be, or is.


> (re:  "feeble" minds)
> I think many of these people have the _potential_ to think for
> themselves, to widen their intellectual horizons, but for whatever
> reason(s) have not reached their full potential.

    Ok, that was another diagnosis, now what is your proposal?


> << How can you be certain that McCarthyism lasted only a few years?
> More likely the same McCarthyism was driven underground and sublimated
> into a corrosive litmus-test of politically "correct/incorrect," eh?
>>

> Oh, please, is being called a "commie" really as devastating as being
> called a racist, today? Do you remember the OJ Simpson trial? Saying
> "nigger" became worse than committing a murder.  Mike Tyson has a
> tattoo of Mao Tse-tung on his arm, yet no one says anything.  Imagine
> if a white boxer had a tattoo of Adolf Hitler or Mussolini.  What a
> fuss the PC'ers would make! By all accounts Mao is responsible for
> more civilian deaths than Hitler and Mussolini combined.  But, oh
> yeah, those Chinese landowners and peasants were not God's Chosen,
> so they don't count.

     Trying to follow your tenous "thread" of logic:  were you saying
  that being called a "commie" -should- be more devastating in light of
  uncontested accounts?  So McCarthyism still simmers on your burner?
  I think that was my point exactly.


> (re: "hatred" towards mother-killers)
> You need to get a clue.  I implied, if this individual cared for his
> mother to any infinitesimal degree, manifesting hatred towards the
> killer would have been a sign of health.

     Even if "hatred" for the sinner, rather than the sin, were to
   improve your effective response, why would we need to spell out a
   "_right_ to hate" using formal legalistic terms?  Does one require
   non-specific "right" in order to manifest hatred?  Seems to me an
   oxymoron and _non-sequitur_.  Hate exists even without "rights."


> << Alright, let's go there. How many "races" are there? On what
> source of information did you base your assessment? What of the
> prospect and evidence of interbreeding? When is "racial purity"
> achieved if Hitler was 25% Jewish? >>

> Rationalization.  Funny, people like you who are eager to deny the
> existence of race are usually the most race conscious.  One guy who
> was arguing with me over the existence/non-existence of race, had his
> handle as "Sixftblkman".  Another would repeatedly refer to whites as
> "crackers."

    These are strawmen.  I don't deny the existence of race, nor of
  implicit racism which follows from racial distinctions.  Even the
  notion of being "color-blind" implies some "colorization" out there
  from which one is assuming deliberate blindness.  My difficulty
  occurs when I'm trying to resolve all cases of people into what may
  seem to be rather arbitrary and -temporal- indicators of racial
  distinction.  There seem to be increasing numbers that do not fit
  nicely into their proper pigeonholes, so the "race" concept is not
  a well-formed notion.  The web-link you've provided also sources
  other documents that more precisely target a "Bayesian statistical
  analysis" of racial phenotype differences.  However, as an employer
  I'd be presented with an individual who was not considered in the
  cited study, and furthermore the impacted minorities who follow up
  such studies are likely to take pains to obliterate former conceptual
  categories, so that the former divisiveness instead becomes blurred.
  For example, if someone is criticized as "not being sufficiently
  educated" in a certain context (an IQ-test) they may 'retaliate' by
  educating themselves in that manner so as to satisfy the requirements
  and diminish the validity of former findings.  So today we have many
  minority lawyers, doctors, engineers, computer programmers, and Chess
  players.  Unless you're prepared to defeat Grandmaster Maurice Ashley
  at Chess, I don't think you've got a strong argument on the IQ-side.

    However, the IQ-test argument was itself premised upon whether a
  given individual, or class of individuals, finds some means of "fit"
  within the corporate "industrial-technological system" that TK rails
  against.  TK is saying the ITS has failed us, is failing us, and will
  itself fail someday, perhaps dooming planetary life to extinction.
  His thesis is that if sustainable 'survival' will be our long-term
  objective then the ITS needs to be revamped, revised, reformed, or
  tossed entirely, to be replaced by some agrarian model that does not
  consume or waste non-renewable resources and does not support the
  dubious agenda of overpopulation/war/poverty cycles, or Spenglerian
  rise and fall of civilizations, because today's methods of warfare
  have moved the debate into a twilight-zone realm that does not exempt
  civilians from international conflict.  IQ has meaning only if it is
  inextricably tied to the survival of individuals, groups and society.
  In the context of a dysfunctional economic model, IQ mensuration will
  itself be contributory to that same dysfunctionality.  Focusing upon
  IQ diverts attention from the real-world issues which are strictly
  those of 'survivability' and 'sustainable survival' for an indefinite
  future.  If human beings annihilate each other in nuclear holocaust,
  _at_any_future_time_, then the 'meek' insects who shall inherit this
  Earth will, for all intents and purposes, be those truly intelligent
  survivors.  Such are the "rules of the game" imposed by that blind
  and impersonal watchmaker called evolution.  Everything that survives
  has equivalent "intelligence" to everything else; so -that- is the
  central "irony" occupying each and every thread of an IQ discourse.

    Now here's a web-link for you:

        http://virtual.park.uga.edu/~232/voc.html
        -----------------------------------------



        - regards
        - jb
